questions.q: Creative thinking is the ability to generate ____ ideas.
questions.explanation: Creative thinking involves generating ideas that are novel or unconventional and also useful or appropriate, so innovative, unconventional and useful all describe creative ideas.

questions.q: ____ are representative items within each concept.
questions.explanation: A prototype is the most typical or best example of a concept, against which new items are compared to decide category membership.

questions.q: A mental representation can take the form of a ____.
questions.explanation: Mental representations can be verbal (words), visual or other images, and sounds, among other forms, so all of the given apply.

questions.q: Which of the following is true?
options: Thinking is a lower mental process
Thinking is unrelated to problem solving
We can only think in numbers or words
questions.explanation: Watson, a behaviorist, described thinking as sub-vocal talking, i.e., inner speech involving small movements of the speech organs. Thinking is actually a higher mental process closely tied to problem solving and can use images as well as words.

questions.q: Cognitive architecture is a theory about the ____ that create a mind in natural or artificial systems.
questions.explanation: Cognitive architecture is a theory of the fixed structures (memory stores, processing modules and their organization) that give rise to a mind, whether natural or artificial, such as ACT-R or Soar.

questions.q: Bloom's Taxonomy is a system of hierarchical models (arranged in a hierarchical rank,) used to categorize ____ into varying levels of complexity.
questions.explanation: Bloom's taxonomy classifies educational learning objectives into hierarchical levels of complexity, from remembering up to creating in the revised version.

questions.q: ____ knowledge refers to knowledge of terminology and specific details.
questions.explanation: In the revised Bloom's taxonomy, factual knowledge is the basic elements a learner must know: terminology and specific details. Conceptual knowledge concerns relationships, and metacognitive knowledge concerns awareness of one's own cognition.

questions.q: Choosing to skim subheadings of unimportant information to get to the information we need as a metacognitive skill is called ____.
questions.explanation: Skimming means quickly scanning headings and subheadings to skip unimportant material and locate needed information, which is a deliberate, strategic metacognitive reading skill.

questions.q: ____ refers to the ability to regulate your thoughts and set aside any personal biases to come to the best conclusion.
questions.explanation: In lists of critical thinking skills, self-regulation is described as monitoring and regulating one's own thinking and setting aside personal biases to reach the best conclusion. Open-mindedness is related but refers to being receptive to different viewpoints.

questions.q: ____ method of solving problems refers to a rule that guarantees the solution to a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step rule or procedure that guarantees a correct solution if followed, though it may be slow. Heuristics, analogies and trial and error do not guarantee a solution.
